text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers often clean up messy code to make it easier to read and understand. Good refactoring makes programs simpler, so other people can work with them more easily. It also helps reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly and poorly. By refactoring regularly, teams keep their projects healthy and avoid bigger problems in the future. Remember, the goal is to make the code better, not to add new features.
